evals.prompt: Make a few polished slides about safe database migrations for junior backend developers.
evals.expected_output: Marp Markdown with suitable technical theme, lead title, concise slides, and audience-appropriate content.
assertions: Uses `<!-- _class: lead -->` and `---` slide separators.
Includes safe database migrations and junior backend developers.
Content headings are concise and slides have at most five bullets each.

evals.prompt: Create exactly 5 Marp slides for a developer meetup on diagnosing slow API requests, including tracing and database queries.
evals.expected_output: A five-slide Marp deck built on the tech template, with lead title and requested topics.
assertions: Has `marp: true` frontmatter and exactly five slide sections, excluding frontmatter delimiters.
Keeps the tech template's frontmatter (`theme: default`) and its `<style>` block, and uses `<!-- _class: lead -->` on the title slide.
Includes tracing and database-query content.
Contains no unresolved template placeholders.

evals.expected_output: Requests the missing topic/audience and does not fabricate detailed slides or claim to save a file.
assertions: Asks for a specific topic or audience.
Does not claim a file was saved to `/mnt/user-data/outputs/`.

evals.prompt: Here's my deck for Thursday's incident review (incident-review.md). It feels crowded and the alternating dark slides I set up never show up. Clean it up but don't lose any of the facts. I don't have Marp CLI on this machine.
evals.expected_output: A redesigned incident-review deck that keeps every fact, number, the code line, the image path and the speaker note; splits the nine-bullet slide; shortens the long heading; replaces the dead nth-child rule and the inline style attribute; and says the deck was linted, not rendered. The image file is not supplied, so the path stays and the report flags that it was not verified.
assertions: Keeps every figure from the fixture: 4.18.0, 14:02, 210 ms, 840 ms, 3.2%, 14 minutes, 5%, 14:31, 14:38, 92%, 61%, 312 tickets and 41,000 EUR.
Keeps the `ConnectionPool(max_size=50, timeout_s=2)` code line, the `img/latency-chart.png` image and the speaker-note comment about the 5% threshold.
No slide has more than five bullets, and the long 'What happened...' heading is replaced by a short one-line heading.
Removes the `section:nth-child(2n)` rule and explains that it never matches in Marp; any dark slides use a `<!-- _class: ... -->` directive with a matching `section.<name>` rule.
Replaces the inline `style=` attribute on the 840 ms paragraph with a class or Markdown emphasis, or explains that Marp strips it without `--html`.
Says the deck was checked without rendering (no Marp CLI) and does not claim a visual check.

evals.prompt: Build a 4-slide opener for my design conference keynote, "Calm interfaces", in the gradient style. Put photos/hero.jpg behind the title, give one slide a side-by-side of photos/before.png and photos/after.png, and don't make every slide the same color. I'll export it to PDF with marp.
evals.expected_output: A four-slide deck on the gradient template with a darkened hero background on the title, a two-image bg comparison slide, per-slide warm/teal class variants, and the --allow-local-files flag in the PDF command. The photos are not supplied: the deck uses the given paths and tells the user they must exist next to the deck.
assertions: Has exactly four slide sections, keeps `theme: default` and the gradient template's `<style>` block, and never sets `theme: gradient`.
Varies slide backgrounds with `<!-- _class: warm -->` or `<!-- _class: teal -->` and adds no `section:nth-child` rule.
The title slide uses `![bg ...](photos/hero.jpg)` with a darkening or blur filter (for example `brightness:0.5`) so the white title stays readable.

One slide holds both `photos/before.png` and `photos/after.png` as `bg` images side by side: either both unmarked (full-width split) or sharing one `left`/`right` region; it never marks one image `left` and the other `right`.
The PDF export command includes `--pdf` and `--allow-local-files`, with the reason that local photos are otherwise blank.
